InputRequiredSource
Job to be done, in one sentence, with the success metricyesuser
Actions the system may take (read-only vs write; external side effects)yesuser
Available tools/APIs/data sources and their auth modelyesuser / repo

Latency and cost envelopenouser; mark [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Non-functional constraints (data residency, PII, audit)nouser

If the job statement or the action list is missing, ask once. Never design an agent for an undefined task.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.

How to run

When to use

  • Pre-launch risk review of an AI use case; building or refreshing the AI risk register; model documentation; regulatory mapping at summary level.
  • NOT for: legal opinions (state this; route to counsel), strategy/CoE (ai-strategy-coe), eval mechanics (llm-eval-harness).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Use-case description: purpose, users, decisions influenced, autonomy levelyesuser / design doc
Data: categories (PII, special categories, minors, financial, health, education records), sources, jurisdictionsyesuser
Model(s): provider/open-weights, version, fine-tuned?, hosting locationyesuser
Deployment context: internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated decisionyesuser
Existing controls and policiesnouser
Applicable regulations the org already tracksnouser; otherwise summary mapping only

If the use case, data categories, or deployment context are missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Classify the use case. Determine the internal risk tier (low / medium / high) using references/risk-taxonomy.md §Tiering, and the summary EU AI Act tier using references/regulatory-mapping.md. State both with the criteria met.

AI Strategy & CoE Design

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (portfolio.csv, portfolio.md, maturity.md, roadmap.md); fill the operating-model and governance sections of the roadmap by hand from the references.

When to use

  • "Build our AI strategy", "stand up an AI CoE", "where are we on AI maturity", "prioritize our AI backlog", "12-month AI roadmap".
  • Executive audience: CIO, CDO, CTO, board.
  • NOT for: qualifying one idea (ai-use-case-canvas), risk/compliance only (ai-governance-risk), agent design (agent-architecture).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Organization context (industry, size, regulatory posture)yesuser
Current-state evidence (data platforms, cloud, existing AI/ML, team)yesuser / documents
Candidate use-case list (even rough)nouser; skill elicits if missing
Executive sponsor and budget envelopenouser; mark [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] if absent
Strategic priorities for the next 12 monthsyesuser / annual plan

If organization context or current-state evidence is missing, ask once. Do not infer maturity from industry averages.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Assess maturity. Score each of the five dimensions 1–5 using references/maturity-model.md. Record evidence per score in assets/maturity-scorecard.csv. A score without evidence is [TO BE BASELINED].
  3. Pick the operating model. Apply the decision table in references/operating-models.md. State the chosen model, the two rejected ones, and why. Maturity level and organizational breadth drive this, not preference.
  4. Score the portfolio. Score every candidate use case on value, feasibility, risk, data readiness (1–5 each) with references/use-case-scoring.md; fill assets/use-case-scoring.csv. Compute priority = value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk. Classify: Now / Next / Later / Stop.
  5. Define governance. Minimum: intake gate, risk tiering, model inventory, review cadence. Point deeper controls to ai-governance-risk.
  6. Build the roadmap. Use assets/roadmap.md with references/roadmap-skeleton.md. Q1 is foundations and 1–2 lighthouse use cases; never schedule scale before measurement exists.
  7. Write the executive summary (≤5 bullets): maturity headline, model choice, top-3 use cases, investment envelope or [TO BE BASELINED], first 90-day commitments.
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ai-strategy-<org>.md: exec summary, maturity table, operating model, portfolio table, governance, roadmap, risks, next steps (owner + date).
  • maturity-scorecard.csv and use-case-scoring.csv filled.
  • Saved to the working directory unless the user names a path.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every maturity score has an evidence line or a [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] marker
  • [ ] Operating model choice cites the decision criteria it satisfied
  • [ ] Portfolio table has every candidate scored on all four axes; no "high/med/low" without the numeric score
  • [ ] Roadmap quarters each have an exit criterion and an owner
  • [ ] No vendor named as a recommendation without a stated selection criterion
  • [ ] No invented benchmark figures; industry comparisons carry a source or are omitted
  • [ ] First line is the answer

References

  • references/maturity-model.md — 5-level model with criteria per dimension
  • references/operating-models.md — central / hub-and-spoke / federated, when to choose
  • references/use-case-scoring.md — rubric and formula
  • references/roadmap-skeleton.md — 12-month quarter plan with exit criteria
  • scripts/score_portfolio.py — scoring CSV → ranked portfolio.csv + unscored.csv + portfolio.md
  • scripts/maturity.py — scorecard CSV → maturity.md + roadmap.md skeleton (one item per gap)

# AI Strategy & CoE Design

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-strategy-coe`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (`portfolio.csv`, `portfolio.md`, `maturity.md`, `roadmap.md`); fill the operating-model and governance sections of the roadmap by hand from the references.

## When to use
- "Build our AI strategy", "stand up an AI CoE", "where are we on AI maturity", "prioritize our AI backlog", "12-month AI roadmap".
- Executive audience: CIO, CDO, CTO, board.
- NOT for: qualifying one idea (`ai-use-case-canvas`), risk/compliance only (`ai-governance-risk`), agent design (`agent-architecture`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Organization context (industry, size, regulatory posture) | yes | user |
| Current-state evidence (data platforms, cloud, existing AI/ML, team) | yes | user / documents |
| Candidate use-case list (even rough) | no | user; skill elicits if missing |
| Executive sponsor and budget envelope | no | user; mark `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if absent |
| Strategic priorities for the next 12 months | yes | user / annual plan |

If organization context or current-state evidence is missing, ask once. Do not infer maturity from industry averages.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. **Assess maturity.** Score each of the five dimensions 1–5 using `references/maturity-model.md`. Record evidence per score in `assets/maturity-scorecard.csv`. A score without evidence is `[TO BE BASELINED]`.
3. **Pick the operating model.** Apply the decision table in `references/operating-models.md`. State the chosen model, the two rejected ones, and why. Maturity level and organizational breadth drive this, not preference.
4. **Score the portfolio.** Score every candidate use case on value, feasibility, risk, data readiness (1–5 each) with `references/use-case-scoring.md`; fill `assets/use-case-scoring.csv`. Compute priority = value × feasibility × data readiness ÷ risk. Classify: Now / Next / Later / Stop.
5. **Define governance.** Minimum: intake gate, risk tiering, model inventory, review cadence. Point deeper controls to `ai-governance-risk`.
6. **Build the roadmap.** Use `assets/roadmap.md` with `references/roadmap-skeleton.md`. Q1 is foundations and 1–2 lighthouse use cases; never schedule scale before measurement exists.
7. **Write the executive summary** (≤5 bullets): maturity headline, model choice, top-3 use cases, investment envelope or `[TO BE BASELINED]`, first 90-day commitments.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ai-strategy-<org>.md`: exec summary, maturity table, operating model, portfolio table, governance, roadmap, risks, next steps (owner + date).
- `maturity-scorecard.csv` and `use-case-scoring.csv` filled.
- Saved to the working directory unless the user names a path.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every maturity score has an evidence line or a `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` marker
- [ ] Operating model choice cites the decision criteria it satisfied
- [ ] Portfolio table has every candidate scored on all four axes; no "high/med/low" without the numeric score
- [ ] Roadmap quarters each have an exit criterion and an owner
- [ ] No vendor named as a recommendation without a stated selection criterion
- [ ] No invented benchmark figures; industry comparisons carry a source or are omitted
- [ ] First line is the answer

## References
- `references/maturity-model.md` — 5-level model with criteria per dimension
- `references/operating-models.md` — central / hub-and-spoke / federated, when to choose
- `references/use-case-scoring.md` — rubric and formula
- `references/roadmap-skeleton.md` — 12-month quarter plan with exit criteria
- `scripts/score_portfolio.py` — scoring CSV → ranked `portfolio.csv` + `unscored.csv` + `portfolio.md`
- `scripts/maturity.py` — scorecard CSV → `maturity.md` + `roadmap.md` skeleton (one item per gap)

Infra & GPU Sizing (inference)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/infra-gpu-sizing --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/infra-gpu-sizing). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • Sizing inference capacity for a self-hosted or rented LLM/SLM; deciding self-host vs rental vs API; budgeting a pilot or rollout.
  • NOT for: training/fine-tuning cluster sizing, picking a model (use evals), network/storage design.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Concurrent or daily active users and peak factoryesuser
Requests per user per day; tokens in/out per request (averages)yesuser / logs; if absent ask, then state assumptions
Latency SLO: time-to-first-token and tokens/s per stream, or end-to-end p95yesuser
Model(s) and precision (e.g., 8B at fp16/int8), context lengthyesuser
Measured or vendor-stated throughput: tokens/s per GPU for that model + serving stackyesuser benchmark or vendor doc; not invented by the skill
Unit prices: $/GPU-hr rental, self-host capex and power/hosting, API $/1M tokensyesuser; dated
Availability target, residency, data constraintsnouser

If throughput per GPU or unit prices are missing, ask once; otherwise run with explicitly labeled placeholder inputs and mark results illustrative.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Build the workload model with references/workload-model.md: requests/day → peak requests/s → tokens/s required (prefill and decode separated).
  3. Compute capacity with references/throughput-math.md: GPUs = ceil(peak tokens/s ÷ effective tokens/s per GPU ÷ utilization target) with headroom for redundancy. Latency check: decode tokens/s per stream vs SLO at the resulting concurrency.

  5. Apply TCO factors with references/tco-factors.md: utilization, ops staffing, upgrade cycle, egress, support, idle time, scaling elasticity.
  6. Recommend: option, GPU count, monthly cost range, breakeven utilization between rental and self-host, and the triggers to revisit.

LLM Eval Harness

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/llm-eval-harness --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/llm-eval-harness). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • Before first release of any LLM feature or agent; before every prompt/model/tool change thereafter.
  • Answering "is it good enough" with numbers instead of demos.
  • NOT for: retrieval tuning alone (rag-pipeline-design), load testing, security pen-testing.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The system under test: how to call it (function, HTTP endpoint, CLI) and its input/output shapeyesuser / repo
What "good" means: the task definition and the failure types the owner fears mostyesuser
Real examples: ≥ 30 inputs with expected outputs or acceptance notesyesuser / logs; if absent, ask — synthetic cases are labeled and capped at 30% of the set
Risk tier (internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated)yesuser
Release cadence and CI systemnorepo

If the system interface or the real examples are missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.
  2. Build the golden set with references/golden-set.md into assets/golden-set.csv: id, input, expected (or acceptance keywords/regex), category, difficulty, must-not-contain, source, weight.
  3. Design the rubric with references/rubric-design.md into assets/eval-rubric.csv: criterion, definition, scale, pass threshold, scoring method (deterministic / judge / human), weight.
  4. Wire the runner. Copy scripts/run_evals.py; implement call_system(input) -> output for the system under test. Default scoring is deterministic (keywords, regex, must-not-contain, exact match, JSON validity). Add an LLM judge only for criteria that cannot be scored deterministically, following references/llm-as-judge.md.
  5. Run baseline. python3 -I scripts/run_evals.py --golden assets/golden-set.csv --rubric assets/eval-rubric.csv --out scorecard.json. Record the baseline per category.
  6. Set the gate with references/regression-gating.md: overall threshold, per-category minimums, zero-tolerance checks (safety, must-not-contain), and max regression vs baseline. Add the runner to CI (pytest collects it).
  7. Report the scorecard: table by category, failures with ids, gate result, recommended fixes.
  8. Run the self-check.

# LLM Eval Harness

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/llm-eval-harness --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/llm-eval-harness`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## When to use
- Before first release of any LLM feature or agent; before every prompt/model/tool change thereafter.
- Answering "is it good enough" with numbers instead of demos.
- NOT for: retrieval tuning alone (`rag-pipeline-design`), load testing, security pen-testing.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The system under test: how to call it (function, HTTP endpoint, CLI) and its input/output shape | yes | user / repo |
| What "good" means: the task definition and the failure types the owner fears most | yes | user |
| Real examples: ≥ 30 inputs with expected outputs or acceptance notes | yes | user / logs; if absent, ask — synthetic cases are labeled and capped at 30% of the set |
| Risk tier (internal / employee-facing / customer-facing / regulated) | yes | user |
| Release cadence and CI system | no | repo |

If the system interface or the real examples are missing, ask once.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`.
2. **Build the golden set** with `references/golden-set.md` into `assets/golden-set.csv`: id, input, expected (or acceptance keywords/regex), category, difficulty, must-not-contain, source, weight.
3. **Design the rubric** with `references/rubric-design.md` into `assets/eval-rubric.csv`: criterion, definition, scale, pass threshold, scoring method (deterministic / judge / human), weight.
4. **Wire the runner.** Copy `scripts/run_evals.py`; implement `call_system(input) -> output` for the system under test. Default scoring is deterministic (keywords, regex, must-not-contain, exact match, JSON validity). Add an LLM judge only for criteria that cannot be scored deterministically, following `references/llm-as-judge.md`.
5. **Run baseline.** `python3 -I scripts/run_evals.py --golden assets/golden-set.csv --rubric assets/eval-rubric.csv --out scorecard.json`. Record the baseline per category.
6. **Set the gate** with `references/regression-gating.md`: overall threshold, per-category minimums, zero-tolerance checks (safety, must-not-contain), and max regression vs baseline. Add the runner to CI (pytest collects it).
7. **Report** the scorecard: table by category, failures with ids, gate result, recommended fixes.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `assets/golden-set.csv`, `assets/eval-rubric.csv` filled; `scripts/run_evals.py` adapted; `scorecard.json`; CI job snippet.

- [ ] Every rubric criterion has a scoring method and threshold
- [ ] Deterministic checks used wherever possible; judge only where needed, with calibration plan
- [ ] Zero-tolerance checks defined for the risk tier
- [ ] Gate fails the build on threshold or regression breach
- [ ] Baseline recorded with model/prompt version
- [ ] No quality claims without the scorecard

How to run

The runner then runs the scaffold's own pytest suite as a check; implement the stubs afterwards, following the Procedure.

When to use

  • Building a new MCP server (Python or TypeScript), wrapping an existing API/database/SaaS as MCP tools, or reviewing a server for spec compliance and safety.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Target system(s) to expose and their API/docsyesuser / repo / URL
Tool list with side-effect class (read / write / irreversible / external_comm)yesuser; derive with agent-architecture if absent
Language and transport (stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote)yesuser; default Python + stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote
Auth model (API key, OAuth, service account) and tenant modelyesuser
Consumers (Claude Desktop/Code, custom agent, gateway)nouser

If the target system or the tool list is missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.
  2. Choose the implementation path. If the Anthropic mcp-builder skill is installed (see VENDORED.md at the repo root), use it for scaffolding and SDK specifics; else follow references/mcp-spec-essentials.md, which is a complete fallback covering protocol primitives, tool schemas, transports, auth, errors, and testing.
  3. Design tool contracts first. One JSON contract per tool using assets/tool-contract.schema.json (same template as agent-architecture). Apply the rules in references/mcp-spec-essentials.md §3: narrow tools, additionalProperties: false, enums, pagination, structured errors, side-effect metadata.
  4. Scaffold per references/server-skeleton.md: layout, config, logging, health, tests. Keep business logic in a service layer; the MCP layer only validates, authorizes, calls, and shapes output.

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/rag-pipeline-design --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/rag-pipeline-design). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • New knowledge assistant, document Q&A, policy/contract search, support knowledge base, code or ticket search.
  • Diagnosing a RAG system that answers wrong, hallucinates, or costs too much.
  • NOT for: fine-tuning decisions, agent control flow (agent-architecture), full answer-quality harness (llm-eval-harness; this skill covers retrieval metrics and hands off).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Corpus description: types, count, size, update rate, languages, access controlyesuser
Question types with 10+ real examplesyesuser; if absent, ask — synthetic questions are a last resort and labeled
Users, volume (queries/day), latency SLOyesuser; mark [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] if unknown
Freshness requirement (how stale may an answer be)yesuser
Constraints: residency, PII, allowed vendors, budgetnouser

If the corpus or example questions are missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md.
  2. Decide whether RAG is the right tool. Small, static corpus that fits the context window → direct context, no retrieval. Structured data → SQL/API tool, not embeddings. Record the decision.
  3. Design ingestion and chunking with references/chunking-strategies.md: parser per document type, chunk strategy per type, metadata schema (source, section, ACL, timestamp, version), dedup, update/delete path.
  4. Select embeddings and index with references/embedding-selection.md: criteria table (domain fit, language, dimension/cost, latency, licensing, hosting), index type, ACL filtering strategy.
  5. Design retrieval with references/retrieval-and-reranking.md: hybrid (BM25 + dense) by default, metadata filters, query rewriting, reranker, k values, context assembly, citation format.
  6. Build the eval set (assets/retrieval-eval-set.csv): ≥ 50 queries with expected doc/chunk ids; run scripts/eval_retrieval.py for recall@k and MRR. Define answer-level metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance) with references/eval-metrics.md; hand off scoring to llm-eval-harness.

  8. Model cost with references/cost-model.md and assets/cost-model-inputs.csv: ingestion, storage, query (embedding + retrieval + rerank + generation), re-indexing. All unit prices are user inputs; none are hardcoded.

  10. Run the self-check.

Output

  • rag-design-<name>.md plus filled retrieval-eval-set.csv and cost-model-inputs.csv.

handoff-and-thread-close

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/handoff-and-thread-close --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/handoff-and-thread-close). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Every changed file comes from git diff --name-status; copy the result to docs/HANDOFF.md (or pass --write-to-repo to the script) and commit it so the next run knows where this thread ended.

When to use

  • End of a thread; topic change (rule: one topic per thread); context window filling; before a long pause.
  • After any build skill finishes its verify gate.
  • NOT for: writing the PR itself (the PR template covers that), changelogs.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Repo with docs/HANDOFF.md (create from assets/HANDOFF.md if missing)yesrepo
Git state (git status, git diff --stat, recent commits)yesrepo
What was attempted and what remains (from the thread)yesthread
Verification results (commands run and outcomes)yesthread — if not run, run them now

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md (HANDOFF contract, rules 5 and 7) and references/handoff-method.md.
  2. Collect facts from git, not memory. git status --short, git diff --stat main...HEAD (or since last HANDOFF commit), git log --oneline -10. Every changed file in the handoff comes from this list.
  3. Verify or declare. Run lint / typecheck / unit / build if not run in this thread. Record results. If something is red, the state line says so first. (gate: verify)
  4. Write HANDOFF.md per assets/HANDOFF.md: State (one line, honest), Done this thread, Changed files (path — why), Open items (owner), Decisions made (with ADR links if any), Next thread starts with (an exact prompt that names the files to read and the first action).
  5. Prune. Remove items from previous threads that are done; keep the file ≤ 80 lines. Older history lives in git.
  6. Changed-files list in chat (≤ 15 lines) for commit/PR; flag any file changed that is outside the thread's topic (should it be reverted or split?).
  7. Thread summary in chat: ≤ 50 words, bottom line first.
  8. Offer the commit command (git add <files> && git commit -m "<type>: <msg>") — do not run it unless asked.

| Git state (`git status`, `git diff --stat`, recent commits) | yes | repo |
| What was attempted and what remains (from the thread) | yes | thread |
| Verification results (commands run and outcomes) | yes | thread — if not run, run them now |

If a required input is missing, ask for it once; do not guess.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md` (HANDOFF contract, rules 5 and 7) and `references/handoff-method.md`.
2. **Collect facts from git, not memory.** `git status --short`, `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (or since last HANDOFF commit), `git log --oneline -10`. Every changed file in the handoff comes from this list.
3. **Verify or declare.** Run lint / typecheck / unit / build if not run in this thread. Record results. If something is red, the state line says so first. *(gate: verify)*
4. **Write HANDOFF.md** per `assets/HANDOFF.md`: State (one line, honest), Done this thread, Changed files (path — why), Open items (owner), Decisions made (with ADR links if any), Next thread starts with (an exact prompt that names the files to read and the first action).
5. **Prune.** Remove items from previous threads that are done; keep the file ≤ 80 lines. Older history lives in git.
6. **Changed-files list** in chat (≤ 15 lines) for commit/PR; flag any file changed that is outside the thread's topic (should it be reverted or split?).
7. **Thread summary** in chat: ≤ 50 words, bottom line first.
8. Offer the commit command (`git add <files> && git commit -m "<type>: <msg>"`) — do not run it unless asked.

## Output
| Artifact | Path / form |
|---|---|
| HANDOFF | `docs/HANDOFF.md` |
| Changed files | chat list |
| Next-thread prompt | inside HANDOFF; also pasted in chat as a code block |
| Commit command | chat |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every changed file came from `git status/diff`, not recollection
- [ ] State line is true (green/red/partial) and first
- [ ] Each open item has an owner
- [ ] Next-thread prompt is copy-paste ready and names files to read first
- [ ] HANDOFF ≤ 80 lines; stale items removed
- [ ] Off-topic changes flagged
- [ ] No secrets, no personal details, no chat transcript pasted

- `assets/HANDOFF.md` — the contract template
- `assets/next-thread-prompt.md` — prompt patterns per situation

  3. Build. Run the scaffold — it never overwrites: `` python3 -I scripts/scaffold.py --target <dir> --name "<project>" [--multi-tenant] ` It writes docs/SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/HANDOFF.md, docs/adr/0000-template.md, docs/adr/0001-stack.md, .env.example, .github/workflows/{ci,preview,prod}.yml, .github/CODEOWNERS, .github/pull_request_template.md`.

1. Read `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`, `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`, `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.

5. **Green.** Implement the minimum to pass. No extra behaviour.
6. **Refactor** with tests green after each step. Run the full unit suite, not just the new file. *(gate: build→test)*
7. **E2E.** For page/flow changes: Playwright spec from `references/playwright-patterns.md`. If `anthropics:webapp-testing` is installed, invoke it to drive the browser; otherwise follow the patterns file.
8. **Verify.** Coverage ≥ 80% on `server/` (`npm test -- --coverage`); report the table: criterion → test → status. *(gate: test→verify)*
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md`.

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Pyramid table | chat + top of the plan file |
| Unit/integration tests | `tests/unit/**`, `tests/integration/**` |
| E2E | `tests/e2e/<flow>.spec.ts` |
| Configs | `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`, `tests/setup.ts` |
| Fixtures | `tests/fixtures/**` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every acceptance criterion maps to ≥1 test; every test maps to a criterion
- [ ] Tests written before implementation and seen failing first
- [ ] Negative cases: invalid input, forbidden role, cross-tenant, not-found
- [ ] No test depends on another test's state; DB tests reset
- [ ] Full suite green, coverage gate met
- [ ] No mocking of the thing under test; mock only I/O at the boundary

## References
- `references/test-pyramid.md` — layer per feature type, what to mock, fixtures
- `references/tdd-method.md` — red/green/refactor rules (fallback for superpowers)
- `references/playwright-patterns.md` — auth, tenant, selectors, flake control (fallback for webapp-testing)
- `assets/vitest.config.ts`, `assets/playwright.config.ts`, `assets/tests-setup.ts`, `assets/e2e-auth.setup.ts`, `assets/unit-test.example.ts`, `assets/e2e-test.example.ts`

How to run

  • "I have a panel interview Thursday", "grill me for the CIO round", "map my stories to this JD", "draft my 90-day plan", "what should I ask them".
  • Mock-interview mode: user asks to be questioned and scored.
  • NOT for: résumé rewriting (resume-tailor), post-interview thank-you notes (outreach-and-followup), offer decisions (offer-evaluator).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource

Master résuméyes (if story bank is thin)user file; same format as resume-tailor
JD textyesuser paste

Missing story bank: ask once; offer to build it from the master résumé by interviewing the user (one question per bullet). Never fill it from memory.

TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)

  1. Every story, number, title and outcome traces to a story-bank ID [SB-nn] or résumé line [MR-Lnn].
  2. Allowed: reframe a story for a different competency, tighten, pick which details to lead with, add a Reflection sentence the user confirms.
  3. Not allowed: invent a story, add a metric, change the user's role in the story, upgrade "contributed" to "led".
  4. If the JD needs a competency with no story, say so and offer: (a) interview the user for a true example, or (b) prepare an honest "here is the closest experience and how I would approach it" answer.
  5. Output includes a traceability table: competency → story ID → fit (STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.

bodyHtml:
JD Fit Scorer

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/jd-fit-scorer --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain career/jd-fit-scorer). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • User pastes a JD, posting URL text, or recruiter summary and asks "should I apply?", "how well do I fit?", "score this", or "rank these roles".
  • User wants a gap list before tailoring a résumé.
  • NOT for: rewriting the résumé (use resume-tailor), evaluating an offer (use offer-evaluator), or logging the application (use application-tracker).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
JD full text (title, responsibilities, requirements, location, comp if listed)yesuser paste or file
Profile keyword file or master résuméyesassets/profile-keywords.example.txt format; user supplies the real one
Hard constraints (location, travel, remote, comp floor, clearance)nouser; defaults in references/scoring-rubric.md
Target level (Sr Director / VP / CxO)nouser; default Sr Director

If the JD or the profile is missing, ask once. Do not score from memory or from a job title alone.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Parse the JD into three buckets: must-haves (required, "must", years, certifications, degree, clearance), nice-to-haves (preferred, "plus", "ideally"), culture/logistics (location, remote policy, travel, reporting line, team size, comp band, industry).
  3. Normalize each requirement to a short keyword phrase (≤6 words). Collapse duplicates.
  4. Match each requirement against the profile keyword file. Mark MATCH, PARTIAL (adjacent skill or older than 7 years), or GAP. Cite the profile line for every MATCH/PARTIAL; a match with no citation is a GAP.
  5. Scan the JD against references/red-flag-catalog.md. Record each hit with its penalty.
  6. Score using references/scoring-rubric.md. Optional: run scripts/score.py (--jd jd.txt --profile profile.txt) for the deterministic keyword pass, then apply judgement to PARTIALs.
  7. Apply the go/no-go thresholds in references/go-no-go.md. Hard-constraint violations force NO-GO regardless of score.
  8. Produce the output below. Run the self-check.

Output

Markdown, first line is the verdict. Save as fit-<company>-<role>.md if a file is requested.

GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <one-sentence reason>

| Bucket | Weight | Items | Matched | Partial | Gap | Bucket score |
| Red flags | — | <n> hits | penalty −<n> |

Gap table: | Requirement | Bucket | Status | Evidence (profile line) | Mitigation |
Red flags: | Flag | Penalty | JD text |
Next action: apply via … / tailor résumé / ask recruiter X before applying / pass

Self-check

  • [ ] Every MATCH/PARTIAL cites a profile line; none inferred from job titles alone
  • [ ] Weights sum to 100 before penalties; math shown
  • [ ] Hard constraints checked before the score is reported
  • [ ] Gap table includes a mitigation or "accept gap" for every GAP
  • [ ] Verdict is the first line; reply ≤50 words outside the artifact
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; profile comes from the supplied file only

References

  • references/scoring-rubric.md — weights, status values, bucket math
  • references/red-flag-catalog.md — penalties and detection phrases
  • references/go-no-go.md — thresholds and hard-constraint overrides
  • scripts/score.py — offline keyword pass (stdlib only)
  • assets/profile-keywords.example.txt — profile file format (EXAMPLE, fictional)

# JD Fit Scorer

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/jd-fit-scorer --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/jd-fit-scorer`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## When to use
- User pastes a JD, posting URL text, or recruiter summary and asks "should I apply?", "how well do I fit?", "score this", or "rank these roles".
- User wants a gap list before tailoring a résumé.
- NOT for: rewriting the résumé (use `resume-tailor`), evaluating an offer (use `offer-evaluator`), or logging the application (use `application-tracker`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| JD full text (title, responsibilities, requirements, location, comp if listed) | yes | user paste or file |
| Profile keyword file or master résumé | yes | `assets/profile-keywords.example.txt` format; user supplies the real one |
| Hard constraints (location, travel, remote, comp floor, clearance) | no | user; defaults in `references/scoring-rubric.md` |
| Target level (Sr Director / VP / CxO) | no | user; default Sr Director |

If the JD or the profile is missing, ask once. Do not score from memory or from a job title alone.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Parse the JD into three buckets: **must-haves** (required, "must", years, certifications, degree, clearance), **nice-to-haves** (preferred, "plus", "ideally"), **culture/logistics** (location, remote policy, travel, reporting line, team size, comp band, industry).
3. Normalize each requirement to a short keyword phrase (≤6 words). Collapse duplicates.
4. Match each requirement against the profile keyword file. Mark `MATCH`, `PARTIAL` (adjacent skill or older than 7 years), or `GAP`. Cite the profile line for every MATCH/PARTIAL; a match with no citation is a GAP.
5. Scan the JD against `references/red-flag-catalog.md`. Record each hit with its penalty.
6. Score using `references/scoring-rubric.md`. Optional: run `scripts/score.py` (`--jd jd.txt --profile profile.txt`) for the deterministic keyword pass, then apply judgement to PARTIALs.
7. Apply the go/no-go thresholds in `references/go-no-go.md`. Hard-constraint violations force NO-GO regardless of score.
8. Produce the output below. Run the self-check.

## Output
Markdown, first line is the verdict. Save as `fit-<company>-<role>.md` if a file is requested.

```
GO / LEAN GO / LEAN NO / NO-GO — <score>/100 — <one-sentence reason>

| Bucket | Weight | Items | Matched | Partial | Gap | Bucket score |
| Red flags | — | <n> hits | penalty −<n> |

Gap table: | Requirement | Bucket | Status | Evidence (profile line) | Mitigation |
Red flags: | Flag | Penalty | JD text |
Next action: apply via … / tailor résumé / ask recruiter X before applying / pass
```

## Self-check
- [ ] Every MATCH/PARTIAL cites a profile line; none inferred from job titles alone
- [ ] Weights sum to 100 before penalties; math shown
- [ ] Hard constraints checked before the score is reported
- [ ] Gap table includes a mitigation or "accept gap" for every GAP
- [ ] Verdict is the first line; reply ≤50 words outside the artifact
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; profile comes from the supplied file only

## References
- `references/scoring-rubric.md` — weights, status values, bucket math
- `references/red-flag-catalog.md` — penalties and detection phrases
- `references/go-no-go.md` — thresholds and hard-constraint overrides
- `scripts/score.py` — offline keyword pass (stdlib only)
- `assets/profile-keywords.example.txt` — profile file format (EXAMPLE, fictional)

Résumé Tailor (truth-locked)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/resume-tailor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain career/resume-tailor). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • "Tailor my résumé for this JD", "make this ATS-friendly", "rewrite my summary for a VP role", "which keywords am I missing".
  • After jd-fit-scorer returns GO / LEAN GO.
  • NOT for: scoring fit (use jd-fit-scorer), cover letters or recruiter messages (use outreach-and-followup), interview stories (use interview-prep).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Master résumé (full, untailored, with line numbers or stable bullet IDs)yesuser file; format in assets/master-resume.example.md
JD full textyesuser paste
Target title and levelnoJD; default Sr Director
Fit output from jd-fit-scorernoprior step; speeds keyword mapping
Page limit and format (2-page, ATS plain, LinkedIn)nouser; default 2-page ATS plain

If the master résumé is missing, stop and ask for it. Do not build from memory, LinkedIn recollection, or prior conversations.

TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)

  1. The master résumé is the only source of facts: employers, titles, dates, team sizes, budgets, metrics, technologies, awards.
  2. Every tailored bullet carries a source reference [MR-L<line>] or [MR-<bullet-id>].
  3. Allowed transformations: reorder, reword, merge two source bullets, drop detail, change emphasis, swap synonyms for JD keywords when the master résumé supports the underlying fact.
  4. Not allowed: new metrics, inflated numbers, new technologies, new scope, new titles, implied certifications, "led" where the source says "contributed to".
  5. If the user asks to add a claim with no source line, refuse that claim, explain why in one sentence, and offer two options: (a) add the fact to the master résumé first with their confirmation it is true, or (b) phrase the adjacent true fact instead. Continue with the rest of the tailoring.

# Résumé Tailor (truth-locked)

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py career/resume-tailor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain career/resume-tailor`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## When to use
- "Tailor my résumé for this JD", "make this ATS-friendly", "rewrite my summary for a VP role", "which keywords am I missing".
- After `jd-fit-scorer` returns GO / LEAN GO.
- NOT for: scoring fit (use `jd-fit-scorer`), cover letters or recruiter messages (use `outreach-and-followup`), interview stories (use `interview-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Master résumé (full, untailored, with line numbers or stable bullet IDs) | yes | user file; format in `assets/master-resume.example.md` |
| JD full text | yes | user paste |
| Target title and level | no | JD; default Sr Director |
| Fit output from `jd-fit-scorer` | no | prior step; speeds keyword mapping |
| Page limit and format (2-page, ATS plain, LinkedIn) | no | user; default 2-page ATS plain |

If the master résumé is missing, stop and ask for it. Do not build from memory, LinkedIn recollection, or prior conversations.

## TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)
1. The master résumé is the only source of facts: employers, titles, dates, team sizes, budgets, metrics, technologies, awards.
2. Every tailored bullet carries a source reference `[MR-L<line>]` or `[MR-<bullet-id>]`.
3. Allowed transformations: reorder, reword, merge two source bullets, drop detail, change emphasis, swap synonyms for JD keywords **when the master résumé supports the underlying fact**.
4. Not allowed: new metrics, inflated numbers, new technologies, new scope, new titles, implied certifications, "led" where the source says "contributed to".
5. If the user asks to add a claim with no source line, refuse that claim, explain why in one sentence, and offer two options: (a) add the fact to the master résumé first with their confirmation it is true, or (b) phrase the adjacent true fact instead. Continue with the rest of the tailoring.
6. The output must include a traceability table. A bullet with no source row is a defect; remove it before returning.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Number the master résumé lines if not already numbered (`MR-L1`…). Do not alter content.
3. Build the ATS keyword map per `references/ats-keyword-mapping.md`: JD keyword → exact/synonym → master résumé evidence line → placement (summary, core competencies, bullet, skills).
4. Flag JD keywords with no evidence as **UNSUPPORTED**. These go in the gap note to the user, never into the résumé.
5. Rewrite the executive summary (≤4 lines) using only supported keywords; structure per `references/executive-resume-structure.md`.
6. Rewrite bullets with the formula in `references/bullet-formula.md`. Prioritize the 8–12 bullets most relevant to the JD's must-haves; demote the rest. Patterns (not facts) are in `assets/bullet-bank.md`.
7. Produce the before/after diff per `references/diff-format.md`.
8. Produce the traceability table: tailored bullet → `[MR-Lxx]` → transformation type.
9. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

## Output
Markdown file `resume-<company>-<role>.md` containing, in order:
1. Keyword map table (JD keyword | status | evidence | placement)
2. Tailored résumé (ATS plain: no tables, no columns, no graphics, standard headings)
3. Before/after diff
4. Traceability table
5. Unsupported-claims note (what the JD wants that the master résumé cannot support, and what to do about it)

## Self-check
- [ ] Every tailored bullet has a `[MR-…]` source and appears in the traceability table
- [ ] No number, employer, title, date, or technology appears that is absent from the master résumé
- [ ] Any user-requested unsupported claim was refused with an explanation and alternatives
- [ ] Summary ≤4 lines; bullets ≤2 lines each; action verb first; metric present where the source has one
- [ ] ATS plain formatting: standard section names, no tables inside the résumé body, dates as `Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY`
- [ ] Banned words from `writing-style.md` absent (leverage, synergy, robust, seamless, cutting-edge)
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory; everything comes from the supplied master résumé

## References

- `scripts/check_traceability.py` — the TRUTH LOCK gate: exit 1 on an uncited bullet, an unknown id, or a number absent from its cited lines

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/client-research-brief --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/client-research-brief). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • "Research <company> before the pitch on <date>."
  • "What is <account> likely to be spending on in the next 12 months?"
  • "Build a brief on the new CIO at <company>."
  • NOT for: competitor analysis (competitive-positioning), quarterly account strategy (account-plan), call synthesis (discovery-interview).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Company legal/common name, HQ countryyesuser
Purpose: pitch / discovery / proposal / exec meeting, and dateyesuser
Our angle: the service line or initiative we are positioningyesuser
Notes/links file (notes.md or .txt: URLs, pasted excerpts, prior-contact notes)nofile
Named stakeholders to profilenouser
Network access available? (yes/no)yesenvironment

If company name or purpose is missing, ask once. Never guess which company is meant when names collide (ask "Acme Corp (NYSE: ACM) or Acme Ltd (UK)?").

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Scope the brief to the purpose. A discovery brief emphasizes initiatives and pains; a proposal brief emphasizes procurement, incumbents, and financial capacity; an exec-meeting brief emphasizes the individual and their public positions. Use references/research-method.md §1 to pick the emphasis weights.
  2. Build the source plan from references/research-method.md §2 (source tiers: filings > investor materials > regulator/press releases > reputable press > job postings > vendor case studies > social). Decide which tiers are reachable: if no network, only the notes file and user-provided excerpts count as sources; everything else is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___].
  3. Run the skeleton script when a notes file exists: python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "<name>" --out brief.md. It classifies links and excerpts into the brief sections and lists what is still empty. Then fill each section by reading the sources (the script does not fetch).
  4. Extract tech-stack signals using references/tech-signal-playbook.md: job postings (platform names, team sizes), engineering blogs, case studies by vendors, conference talks, open-source repos, status pages, DNS/MX hints if provided. Record each signal with confidence (High / Med / Low) per the playbook rubric; never upgrade confidence without a second independent source.
  5. Decision point — financial capacity. If public: pull revenue, operating margin trend, capex/opex guidance, and any stated cost-out or transformation program from the latest annual/quarterly filing (cite the document and page). If private: state ownership (PE / founder / family), last funding or acquisition event if public, and mark capacity [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. Do not estimate revenue for a private company.
  6. Profile leadership limited to the roles that matter for our angle (CIO/CTO/CDO, the business sponsor, CFO, CISO where security gates apply). Tenure, prior employer, public statements, and what they have changed since arrival. Public-record facts only; no inference about personality or politics.

# client-research-brief

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/client-research-brief --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/client-research-brief`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## When to use
- "Research <company> before the pitch on <date>."
- "What is <account> likely to be spending on in the next 12 months?"
- "Build a brief on the new CIO at <company>."
- NOT for: competitor analysis (`competitive-positioning`), quarterly account strategy (`account-plan`), call synthesis (`discovery-interview`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Company legal/common name, HQ country | yes | user |
| Purpose: pitch / discovery / proposal / exec meeting, and date | yes | user |
| Our angle: the service line or initiative we are positioning | yes | user |
| Notes/links file (`notes.md` or `.txt`: URLs, pasted excerpts, prior-contact notes) | no | file |
| Named stakeholders to profile | no | user |
| Network access available? (yes/no) | yes | environment |

If company name or purpose is missing, ask once. Never guess which company is meant when names collide (ask "Acme Corp (NYSE: ACM) or Acme Ltd (UK)?").

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Scope the brief to the purpose.** A discovery brief emphasizes initiatives and pains; a proposal brief emphasizes procurement, incumbents, and financial capacity; an exec-meeting brief emphasizes the individual and their public positions. Use `references/research-method.md` §1 to pick the emphasis weights.
2. **Build the source plan** from `references/research-method.md` §2 (source tiers: filings > investor materials > regulator/press releases > reputable press > job postings > vendor case studies > social). Decide which tiers are reachable: if no network, only the notes file and user-provided excerpts count as sources; everything else is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
3. **Run the skeleton script** when a notes file exists: `python3 -I scripts/brief_skeleton.py --notes notes.md --company "<name>" --out brief.md`. It classifies links and excerpts into the brief sections and lists what is still empty. Then fill each section by reading the sources (the script does not fetch).
4. **Extract tech-stack signals** using `references/tech-signal-playbook.md`: job postings (platform names, team sizes), engineering blogs, case studies by vendors, conference talks, open-source repos, status pages, DNS/MX hints if provided. Record each signal with confidence (High / Med / Low) per the playbook rubric; never upgrade confidence without a second independent source.
5. **Decision point — financial capacity.** If public: pull revenue, operating margin trend, capex/opex guidance, and any stated cost-out or transformation program from the latest annual/quarterly filing (cite the document and page). If private: state ownership (PE / founder / family), last funding or acquisition event if public, and mark capacity `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Do not estimate revenue for a private company.
6. **Profile leadership** limited to the roles that matter for our angle (CIO/CTO/CDO, the business sponsor, CFO, CISO where security gates apply). Tenure, prior employer, public statements, and what they have changed since arrival. Public-record facts only; no inference about personality or politics.
7. **Derive likely initiatives** as hypotheses, not facts: each row cites the signal(s) behind it and states what question on the call would confirm it. Feed these to `discovery-interview`.
8. **Write the brief** on `assets/brief-template.md`. One page. Bottom line first: the three facts the reader must walk in knowing. Sources appendix lists every URL/document with the date accessed.
9. Run the self-check. Delete any sentence you cannot trace to a source line or to the user's notes.

## Output
- File: `client-brief-<company-slug>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections (template order): Bottom line · Snapshot · Financial signals · Technology signals (table with confidence) · Leadership · Recent news (≤6 items, dated) · Likely initiatives and hypotheses · Risks and landmines · Questions for the call · Sources
- Length: ≤ 1 page body plus sources. If longer, move detail to an appendix.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every number carries a source (document + page/section, or URL + date)
- [ ] No revenue, headcount, or spend estimate for a private company unless from a cited public source
- [ ] Tech signals carry a confidence rating; no "they use X" at Low confidence
- [ ] Leadership section contains only public-record facts; no personal characterizations
- [ ] Likely initiatives are labeled hypotheses with the confirming question
- [ ] No content from other clients or from the author's own history
- [ ] Bottom line is three facts, first lines of the document

## References
- `references/research-method.md` — emphasis by purpose, source tiers, financial-signal extraction, writing rules
- `references/tech-signal-playbook.md` — where tech-stack signals live and how to rate confidence
- `assets/brief-template.md` — one-page brief template
- `scripts/brief_skeleton.py` — notes/links file → brief skeleton with empty-section report (no network)

competitive-positioning

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/competitive-positioning --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/competitive-positioning). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • "How do we beat the incumbent at <client>?"
  • "Build a battle card against <competitor type> for this pursuit."
  • "The client's platform vendor is bidding services too — what is our angle?"
  • NOT for: researching the client (client-research-brief), writing the proposal (proposal-writer), rehearsing objections live (orals-prep uses this output).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Pursuit context: client, initiative, decision criteria known, decision owneryesdiscovery synthesis / user
Alternative(s) we face: named competitor, incumbent, vendor services arm, in-house build, status quoyesuser
Evidence about the alternative: public materials, client statements, RFP wording, prior encountersno (but confidence drops without it)files / user
Our cleared proof points and capability catalogyesfile / user
Client's stated priorities and pains (from discovery)yesdiscovery synthesis

If the alternative is unknown, ask once; if still unknown, build the card against "status quo" and "an incumbent-type provider" as labeled hypotheses.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Classify the alternative per references/competitive-method.md §1 (incumbent services provider, platform vendor services, global SI, boutique, in-house, status quo). Each class has predictable strengths, weaknesses, and selling motions; use them as hypotheses, labeled as such, until evidence confirms.
  2. Build the evidence table for the alternative: every strength/weakness claim carries a source (public material, client quote, RFP wording that mirrors their language, prior encounter) and a confidence rating. No evidence → Hypothesis (class pattern); it never becomes a "fact" in any client-facing document.
  3. Map the client's decision criteria (stated in RFP/discovery; else [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]) and score us vs the alternative on each, honestly, using the scoring in §3 of the method. Where we lose on a criterion, decide: neutralize (close the gap), reframe (change the criterion's weight in the client's mind), or concede (do not fight it; move the battle).
  4. Decision point — the wedge. Identify the one or two criteria where we win and the client cares (from discovery). If no such intersection exists, say so: the recommendation is to reshape the opportunity (phase, scope, partner) or to qualify out. Do not manufacture a wedge.
  5. Landmines: what we must not say or do (attacking the incumbent by name, disparaging the platform the client already bought, promising what their contract forbids, referencing other clients without clearance). Add client-specific sensitivities from discovery.
  6. Objection handling with references/objection-handling.md: for each likely objection (the alternative's strengths restated as client concerns), write acknowledge → reframe → proof → ask-back. Proof only from cleared references.
  7. Ghost lines for proposal-writer: the alternative's weakness stated as a general risk the client should evaluate, followed by how we remove it. No names.
  8. Evaluation criteria we want adopted: three to five criteria phrased neutrally that favor our wedge; these go into clarification questions, discovery follow-ups, and the proposal's approach section.
  9. Write the battle card on assets/battle-card-template.md. One page; internal only; marked so. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: battle-card-<client>-vs-<alternative>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md (internal, not for client distribution)
  • Sections: Bottom line (win/lose assessment and wedge in two sentences) · Alternative profile (class, evidence table with confidence) · Criteria scorecard (us vs them with neutralize/reframe/concede) · Wedge · Landmines · Objection handling · Ghost lines · Evaluation criteria to seed · Intelligence gaps (what we need to learn, owner)

Self-check

  • [ ] Every claim about the alternative has a source and confidence, or is labeled hypothesis
  • [ ] Scorecard is honest: at least one criterion where we lose is acknowledged
  • [ ] Wedge sits at the intersection of "we win" and "client cares (sourced)"; or the card says there is none
  • [ ] No competitor named in ghost lines or any content intended for client-facing use
  • [ ] Objection proofs are cleared references only
  • [ ] Landmines include client-specific sensitivities
  • [ ] Card marked internal; no other-client specifics beyond cleared proof; no author history

References

  • references/competitive-method.md — alternative classes, evidence standards, criteria scoring, wedge logic, win/loss patterns
  • references/objection-handling.md — objection patterns by alternative class with response structure
  • assets/battle-card-template.md — one-page battle card

bodyHtml:
discovery-interview

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/discovery-interview --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/discovery-interview). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
  • "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
  • "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
  • NOT for: company background before a pitch (client-research-brief), RFP question lists (rfp-compliance-matrix), or pitch rehearsal (orals-prep).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other)yesuser
Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger eventyesuser / brief
Attendee list with titles (or "unknown")nouser
Mode: prep (before call) or synthesize (after call)yesuser
Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only)yes in synthesizefile
Time available for the call (minutes)no — default 45user

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. Both apply to every output here.

Mode A — prep

  1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use references/question-banks/retail.md as the structural base and say so.
  2. Write 3–5 hypotheses before writing questions (references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
  3. Load the vertical bank from references/question-banks/<vertical>.md. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
  4. Order questions using the funnel in references/discovery-method.md §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
  5. Add the five non-negotiable closes from references/discovery-method.md §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
  6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

Mode B — synthesize

  1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was not said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
  2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in references/discovery-method.md §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], never a guessed number.
  3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
  4. Build the gaps list: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
  5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in references/discovery-method.md §5. Output one of PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
  6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

Both modes

  1. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

Output

ModeFileFormat
prepdiscovery-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.mdSections: Hypotheses (table) · Question plan (table: #, question, persona, hypothesis, time) · Branches · Closes · Pre-reads to send
synthesizediscovery-synthesis-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.mdSections: Bottom line (qualification call) · Pain/Impact/Urgency matrix · Hypothesis register · Gaps list (table with owners) · Follow-up note · Parked items

Template: assets/discovery-pack-template.md.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every question maps to a hypothesis; no orphan questions
  • [ ] No number in the synthesis that is not a verbatim quote or marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
  • [ ] Five closes present (prep) or answered/gapped (synthesize)
  • [ ] Qualification call stated on line 1 of the synthesis
  • [ ] Gaps list has an owner for every row
  • [ ] Follow-up note contains no internal commentary and no other-client references
  • [ ] Tables for questions, matrix, hypotheses, gaps

References

  • references/discovery-method.md — funnel, scoring rubric, closes, qualification gate
  • references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md — hypothesis writing, listening-for-absence, synthesis patterns
  • references/question-banks/edtech.md, references/question-banks/retail.md, references/question-banks/manufacturing.md, references/question-banks/travel.md — vertical banks
  • assets/discovery-pack-template.md — output template

# discovery-interview

## How to run
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/discovery-interview --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/discovery-interview`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

## When to use
- "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
- "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
- "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
- NOT for: company background before a pitch (`client-research-brief`), RFP question lists (`rfp-compliance-matrix`), or pitch rehearsal (`orals-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other) | yes | user |
| Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger event | yes | user / brief |
| Attendee list with titles (or "unknown") | no | user |
| Mode: `prep` (before call) or `synthesize` (after call) | yes | user |
| Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only) | yes in synthesize | file |
| Time available for the call (minutes) | no — default 45 | user |

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. Both apply to every output here.

### Mode A — prep
1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use `references/question-banks/retail.md` as the structural base and say so.
2. Write 3–5 **hypotheses** before writing questions (`references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md` §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
3. Load the vertical bank from `references/question-banks/<vertical>.md`. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
4. Order questions using the funnel in `references/discovery-method.md` §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
5. Add the five **non-negotiable closes** from `references/discovery-method.md` §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

### Mode B — synthesize
1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was *not* said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in `references/discovery-method.md` §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never a guessed number.
3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
4. Build the **gaps list**: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in `references/discovery-method.md` §5. Output one of `PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK` with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

### Both modes
7. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

## Output
| Mode | File | Format |
|---|---|---|
| prep | `discovery-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Hypotheses (table) · Question plan (table: #, question, persona, hypothesis, time) · Branches · Closes · Pre-reads to send |
| synthesize | `discovery-synthesis-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Bottom line (qualification call) · Pain/Impact/Urgency matrix · Hypothesis register · Gaps list (table with owners) · Follow-up note · Parked items |

Template: `assets/discovery-pack-template.md`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every question maps to a hypothesis; no orphan questions
- [ ] No number in the synthesis that is not a verbatim quote or marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Five closes present (prep) or answered/gapped (synthesize)
- [ ] Qualification call stated on line 1 of the synthesis
- [ ] Gaps list has an owner for every row
- [ ] Follow-up note contains no internal commentary and no other-client references
- [ ] Tables for questions, matrix, hypotheses, gaps

## References
- `references/discovery-method.md` — funnel, scoring rubric, closes, qualification gate
- `references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md` — hypothesis writing, listening-for-absence, synthesis patterns
- `references/question-banks/edtech.md`, `references/question-banks/retail.md`, `references/question-banks/manufacturing.md`, `references/question-banks/travel.md` — vertical banks
- `assets/discovery-pack-template.md` — output template

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Decompose to a WBS per references/estimation-method.md §1: phases → work packages → tasks sized 2–15 person-days. Each task carries a driver (count × unit effort) or a fixed effort, a role mix, and a dependency. Keep management, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, and knowledge transfer as explicit packages; they are the most frequently omitted.
  2. Assign 3-point estimates (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic) per task using the calibration rules in §2. Pessimistic is the "things go wrong but not catastrophic" case, typically 1.5–3× most-likely. Record the basis for each: analogy (prior actual), parametric (count × unit), or expert judgment. Expert judgment on >30% of effort is a flag in the output.
  3. Run the model: python3 -I scripts/estimate.py wbs.csv --rates rate-card.csv --iterations 20000 --out estimate.md. Outputs P50/P80/P90 effort and cost, per-phase distribution, staffing table, and a sensitivity list (tasks contributing most variance). Without --rates, the script outputs effort only.
  4. Decision point — confidence level to quote. Per §4: fixed-price → P80 minimum, P90 for migrations with unknown inventories; T&M → P50 as the estimate with P80 as the not-to-exceed; assessments → fixed at P80 with a short duration. State which was used and why.

exec-deck-redline

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/exec-deck-redline --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/exec-deck-redline). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

When to use

  • "Redline this steering-committee deck."
  • "Sharpen these slides for the CIO — keep the story."
  • "Review the board pack before Friday."
  • NOT for: building a new deck (produce content with the domain skill, then this skill for the pass), documents (proposal-writer, sow-drafter).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The deck (PPTX, PDF, or slide text export)yesfile
Audience and the decision the deck must obtainyesuser
Time slot (minutes)yesuser
Source documents behind the numbers (if any)nofiles
Constraints: template, slide limit, mandated sectionsnouser

If the audience or the decision is missing, ask once; a deck without a decision cannot be sharpened, only tidied.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md (redline convention) and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. The user's standing instruction applies: stay close to the original storyline and sharpen it; do not replace the narrative; no invented dollar figures, roles, or dates.

  1. Read the whole deck before touching any slide. Write the storyline as it stands in ≤6 bullets (situation → complication → decision asked → options → recommendation → next steps, or whatever the author used). If the storyline is coherent, it stays. If it has a gap (e.g., no decision slide), that is an [ADD], not a rewrite.
  2. Set the decision test. From the audience and decision input: what must the reader believe after slide 1, and what must they approve by the last slide? Every slide is judged against this.
  3. Score the deck with assets/redline-rubric.md (storyline, titles, evidence, so-what, density, numbers discipline, time fit). Record the score before and after; the after score is the self-check.
  4. Redline slide by slide per references/redline-method.md:
    • [KEEP] unchanged.
    • [SHARPEN] rewrite the title as an assertion; cut to the one point; convert prose to a table or a single chart spec; state the "so what" in the first line of the body. Provide the rewritten text in full.
    • [CUT] with reason (duplicates, no decision relevance, appendix material) and where the content moves.
    • [ADD] only for storyline gaps; state source for any content added.
    • [TBD] for every number, role, date without a source in the provided materials: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___].
  5. Decision point — time fit. Count body slides vs time slot using the rule in the method (§4): roughly one slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck, less for discussion. Over the limit → move to appendix, do not shrink fonts.
  6. Write speaker notes for every kept/sharpened body slide: ≤60 words, the spoken point, the number to say, the transition. Notes never contain content absent from the slide or the sources.
  7. Produce the executive summary slide if missing (one slide: decision asked, three reasons with numbers or [TBD], next steps with owners and dates). Place it as slide 2 (after title) or 1 if there is no title slide.
  8. Deliver: redline table, rewritten slide text in order, speaker notes, parked list (content cut with destination), and the before/after rubric score. If the user supplied a PPTX and asks for the file edited, apply changes with the pptx tooling available in the session; otherwise deliver text ready to paste.
  9. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: deck-redline-<client-or-topic>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md
  • Sections: Storyline as found (≤6 bullets) · Decision test · Rubric score before/after · Redline table (slide #, original title, verdict, reason, new title, body change summary) · Rewritten slides (full text, in order) · Speaker notes · Parked content · Open items ([TBD] list with owners)

Self-check

  • [ ] Storyline preserved; changes are sharpening, not replacement
  • [ ] Every title is an assertion with a number or consequence
  • [ ] Every number, role, date has a source or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
  • [ ] No slide carries more than one point; 3+ items are tables
  • [ ] Slide count fits the time slot; overflow in appendix
  • [ ] Speaker notes ≤60 words, aligned to slide content
  • [ ] Executive summary slide present with decision, reasons, next steps
  • [ ] No banned words; no author or other-client references

References

  • references/redline-method.md — storyline preservation, title assertions, slide patterns, density rules, time fit, speaker-note rules
  • assets/redline-rubric.md — scoring rubric and redline table layout
  • assets/storyline-checklist.md — storyline integrity checklist by deck type

- "Sharpen these slides for the CIO — keep the story."
- "Review the board pack before Friday."
- NOT for: building a new deck (produce content with the domain skill, then this skill for the pass), documents (`proposal-writer`, `sow-drafter`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The deck (PPTX, PDF, or slide text export) | yes | file |
| Audience and the decision the deck must obtain | yes | user |
| Time slot (minutes) | yes | user |
| Source documents behind the numbers (if any) | no | files |
| Constraints: template, slide limit, mandated sections | no | user |

If the audience or the decision is missing, ask once; a deck without a decision cannot be sharpened, only tidied.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` (redline convention) and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. The user's standing instruction applies: stay close to the original storyline and sharpen it; do not replace the narrative; no invented dollar figures, roles, or dates.

1. **Read the whole deck before touching any slide.** Write the storyline as it stands in ≤6 bullets (situation → complication → decision asked → options → recommendation → next steps, or whatever the author used). If the storyline is coherent, it stays. If it has a gap (e.g., no decision slide), that is an `[ADD]`, not a rewrite.
2. **Set the decision test.** From the audience and decision input: what must the reader believe after slide 1, and what must they approve by the last slide? Every slide is judged against this.
3. **Score the deck** with `assets/redline-rubric.md` (storyline, titles, evidence, so-what, density, numbers discipline, time fit). Record the score before and after; the after score is the self-check.
4. **Redline slide by slide** per `references/redline-method.md`:
   - `[KEEP]` unchanged.
   - `[SHARPEN]` rewrite the title as an assertion; cut to the one point; convert prose to a table or a single chart spec; state the "so what" in the first line of the body. Provide the rewritten text in full.
   - `[CUT]` with reason (duplicates, no decision relevance, appendix material) and where the content moves.
   - `[ADD]` only for storyline gaps; state source for any content added.
   - `[TBD]` for every number, role, date without a source in the provided materials: `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Decision point — time fit.** Count body slides vs time slot using the rule in the method (§4): roughly one slide per 2 minutes for a decision deck, less for discussion. Over the limit → move to appendix, do not shrink fonts.
6. **Write speaker notes** for every kept/sharpened body slide: ≤60 words, the spoken point, the number to say, the transition. Notes never contain content absent from the slide or the sources.
7. **Produce the executive summary slide** if missing (one slide: decision asked, three reasons with numbers or `[TBD]`, next steps with owners and dates). Place it as slide 2 (after title) or 1 if there is no title slide.
8. **Deliver**: redline table, rewritten slide text in order, speaker notes, parked list (content cut with destination), and the before/after rubric score. If the user supplied a PPTX and asks for the file edited, apply changes with the pptx tooling available in the session; otherwise deliver text ready to paste.
9. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `deck-redline-<client-or-topic>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections: Storyline as found (≤6 bullets) · Decision test · Rubric score before/after · Redline table (slide #, original title, verdict, reason, new title, body change summary) · Rewritten slides (full text, in order) · Speaker notes · Parked content · Open items (`[TBD]` list with owners)

## Self-check
- [ ] Storyline preserved; changes are sharpening, not replacement
- [ ] Every title is an assertion with a number or consequence
- [ ] Every number, role, date has a source or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No slide carries more than one point; 3+ items are tables
- [ ] Slide count fits the time slot; overflow in appendix
- [ ] Speaker notes ≤60 words, aligned to slide content
- [ ] Executive summary slide present with decision, reasons, next steps
- [ ] No banned words; no author or other-client references

## References
- `references/redline-method.md` — storyline preservation, title assertions, slide patterns, density rules, time fit, speaker-note rules
- `assets/redline-rubric.md` — scoring rubric and redline table layout
- `assets/storyline-checklist.md` — storyline integrity checklist by deck type

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/orals-prep --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain presales/orals-prep). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
