  • "Run a red-team on our pitch."

  • NOT for: fixing the slides (exec-deck-redline), building the battle card (competitive-positioning), writing the proposal (proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The proposal or readout document (final)yesfile
The deck to be presented (final or near-final)yesfile
Format rules: duration, presentation vs Q&A split, attendees (names/roles if known), evaluation criteria, allowed presentersyesRFP / client / user
Our presenting team (names, roles on the engagement)yesuser
Battle card (if a competitive pursuit)nocompetitive-positioning output
Compliance matrix and clarification answers (RFP pursuits)norfp-compliance-matrix output

If format rules or the team are missing, ask once; a script cannot be timed or assigned without them.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Decode the evaluation: from the format rules, list what is scored and by whom. If the evaluation criteria are unknown, mark [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] and assume the proposal's structure is the scoring frame. Map each scored criterion to the slide(s) and speaker that will prove it (references/orals-method.md §1).
  2. Build the timed script on assets/script-template.md: segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, the point (one sentence), the proof (number with source), the transition line. Reserve ≥35% of total time for Q&A unless the format fixes it. Opening ≤90 seconds: their situation, the outcome, what they will hear. Close ≤60 seconds: the ask and the next step.
  3. Assign speakers by credibility, not seniority: the person who will do the work speaks to the approach; the engagement lead to governance and commitments; the executive sponsor opens and closes. Every speaker has ≥1 segment and ≤40% of airtime. Note handoffs explicitly.
  4. Generate the likely-questions bank (references/question-bank-and-red-team.md §1): from the proposal's weak spots (every P/N in the compliance matrix, every [TBD], every assumption), from the evaluation criteria, from the battle card's objections, and from the standard evaluator set. For each: question, who answers, the answer (≤75 words, number + source, no new claims), the evidence slide/page, and the "do not say" line.
  5. Decision point — the hard three. Identify the three questions the team most fears (price, a gap, a credibility challenge). Write the answers with the engagement lead; rehearse these first and most. If an honest answer exposes a real gap, the answer states the gap and the mitigation; it does not spin.
  6. Red-team (§2): assign one person to play the skeptical evaluator and one the incumbent-friendly evaluator; run the objections in the bank plus three unscripted; score with assets/orals-rubric.md; log every answer that exceeded 90 seconds, invented a number, or contradicted the proposal.
  7. Rehearsal plan: dry run 1 (content and timing), dry run 2 (Q&A only), dry run 3 (full, with red team), each with a date and the rubric scores. Fix list after each.
  8. Logistics and risk: room/virtual setup, backups (PDF of deck, offline), who speaks if someone drops, name pronunciation for attendees, prohibited content (other clients' names without clearance, pricing details if sealed).
  9. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: orals-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md
  • Sections: Evaluation map (criterion → slide → speaker) · Timed script · Speaker assignments and handoffs · Likely questions bank (table) · The hard three · Red-team log · Rehearsal plan · Logistics and risks · Open items
  • Companion: assets/orals-rubric.md scored per dry run

Self-check

  • [ ] Every scored criterion mapped to a slide and a speaker
  • [ ] Script timed to the format; Q&A ≥35% unless fixed by the client
  • [ ] Every number in the script and answers traces to the proposal/sources; none new
  • [ ] Hard three identified with honest answers that state gaps and mitigations
  • [ ] Each answer ≤75 words with a named answerer and evidence pointer
  • [ ] No competitor named in any answer; no uncleared client references
  • [ ] Rehearsal plan has dates and rubric scores recorded
  • [ ] Logistics and backups listed

References

  • references/orals-method.md — evaluation decoding, script structure, speaker assignment, answer discipline, delivery rules
  • references/question-bank-and-red-team.md — standard evaluator questions by theme, question-generation sources, red-team protocol
  • assets/script-template.md — timed script layout
  • assets/orals-rubric.md — dry-run scoring rubric

2. **Build the timed script** on `assets/script-template.md`: segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, the point (one sentence), the proof (number with source), the transition line. Reserve ≥35% of total time for Q&A unless the format fixes it. Opening ≤90 seconds: their situation, the outcome, what they will hear. Close ≤60 seconds: the ask and the next step.
3. **Assign speakers by credibility**, not seniority: the person who will do the work speaks to the approach; the engagement lead to governance and commitments; the executive sponsor opens and closes. Every speaker has ≥1 segment and ≤40% of airtime. Note handoffs explicitly.
4. **Generate the likely-questions bank** (`references/question-bank-and-red-team.md` §1): from the proposal's weak spots (every `P`/`N` in the compliance matrix, every `[TBD]`, every assumption), from the evaluation criteria, from the battle card's objections, and from the standard evaluator set. For each: question, who answers, the answer (≤75 words, number + source, no new claims), the evidence slide/page, and the "do not say" line.
5. **Decision point — the hard three.** Identify the three questions the team most fears (price, a gap, a credibility challenge). Write the answers with the engagement lead; rehearse these first and most. If an honest answer exposes a real gap, the answer states the gap and the mitigation; it does not spin.
6. **Red-team** (§2): assign one person to play the skeptical evaluator and one the incumbent-friendly evaluator; run the objections in the bank plus three unscripted; score with `assets/orals-rubric.md`; log every answer that exceeded 90 seconds, invented a number, or contradicted the proposal.
7. **Rehearsal plan**: dry run 1 (content and timing), dry run 2 (Q&A only), dry run 3 (full, with red team), each with a date and the rubric scores. Fix list after each.
8. **Logistics and risk**: room/virtual setup, backups (PDF of deck, offline), who speaks if someone drops, name pronunciation for attendees, prohibited content (other clients' names without clearance, pricing details if sealed).
9. Run the self-check.

- File: `orals-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`

- [ ] Every scored criterion mapped to a slide and a speaker

- [ ] Every number in the script and answers traces to the proposal/sources; none new
- [ ] Hard three identified with honest answers that state gaps and mitigations
- [ ] Each answer ≤75 words with a named answerer and evidence pointer
- [ ] No competitor named in any answer; no uncleared client references
- [ ] Rehearsal plan has dates and rubric scores recorded

InputRequiredSource
RFP document(s): .pdf / .docx / .md / .txt, including appendicesyesfile
Submission deadline, Q&A deadline, format rules (page limits, forms)yes (extract or ask)document / user
Our capability statement or service catalog (what we can claim)yesfile / user
Named owners for response sections (or "assign later")nouser
Known incumbent / competitive contextnouser

If the RFP file is missing, ask once. If the capability source is missing, mark every compliance cell Clarify — owner: ___ rather than guessing what we comply with.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Extract the requirement inventory. Run python3 -I scripts/extract_requirements.py <rfp-file> --out requirements.csv. The script captures numbered clauses (1.2.3, (a), R-014), and sentences with shall / must / required / will provide, with section context and page. Review the CSV: merge split sentences, drop boilerplate (definitions, instructions to bidders go in a separate "Administrative" category), and add any requirements the script missed from tables and appendices. Never renumber the client's IDs; add our REQ-nnn alongside.
  2. Classify every requirement using references/requirement-taxonomy.md: Category (Functional / Technical / Security-Compliance / Commercial / Delivery-PM / Administrative), Mandatory vs Desirable (per RFP wording), and Evaluation weight if the RFP states scoring. Flag "hidden mandatories" — requirements phrased softly but located in pass/fail sections.
  3. Score compliance per references/compliance-scoring.md: C Comply · P Partial · N Non-comply · Q Clarify. The rule: C requires evidence we can cite (project, certification, product feature, named capability in our catalog). No evidence → P or Q, never C. Each row gets an owner and the proposal section that will carry the response.
  4. Decision point — bid/no-bid. Apply the gate in references/compliance-scoring.md §3: any N on a mandatory is a hard stop unless a clarification can convert it; compute C share on mandatories; check deadline feasibility against the response effort (count of sections × owners available). Output BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID with the three facts that drove it. Do not soften a NO-BID.
  5. Draft clarification questions for every Q, ambiguous mandatory, and scoring-rule gap. Use the question format in references/compliance-scoring.md §4: neutral wording, no capability reveal, one question per item, reference the clause ID. Group by theme; cap at the count the RFP allows.
  6. Build the gaps-and-risks list: every P and N with the mitigation (partner, roadmap commitment, alternative approach, exception request) and the risk if unmitigated.
  7. Assemble the matrix on assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md (column spec) — export as CSV/XLSX for the response team, plus a Markdown summary for the bid review. Totals by category and by compliance level must reconcile with the inventory count.
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

ArtifactFileNotes
Requirement inventoryrfp-<client>-requirements.csvScript output, reviewed
Compliance matrixrfp-<client>-compliance-matrix.csv (or .xlsx if openpyxl available)Columns per assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md
Bid review summaryrfp-<client>-bid-review.mdBottom line (BID call) · Totals table · Mandatory non-compliances · Gaps and risks · Clarification questions · Response plan (section, owner, due) · Administrative checklist

Self-check

  • [ ] Inventory count = matrix row count; totals by category reconcile
  • [ ] No C without a cited evidence item
  • [ ] Every mandatory N or P appears in gaps-and-risks with a mitigation and owner
  • [ ] Clarification questions reference clause IDs and reveal no capability gaps
  • [ ] Bid/no-bid call on line 1 of the summary with its three drivers
  • [ ] Deadlines (Q&A, submission) stated with source page
  • [ ] No other-client names or internal rate information in any artifact that could ship

References

  • references/requirement-taxonomy.md — categories, mandatory detection, hidden-mandatory patterns, evaluation weighting
  • references/compliance-scoring.md — C/P/N/Q rules, evidence standard, bid/no-bid gate, clarification-question format
  • assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md — column specification for CSV/XLSX
  • scripts/extract_requirements.py — .txt/.md/.docx/.pdf → requirements CSV

3. **Score compliance** per `references/compliance-scoring.md`: `C` Comply · `P` Partial · `N` Non-comply · `Q` Clarify. The rule: `C` requires evidence we can cite (project, certification, product feature, named capability in our catalog). No evidence → `P` or `Q`, never `C`. Each row gets an owner and the proposal section that will carry the response.
4. **Decision point — bid/no-bid.** Apply the gate in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §3: any `N` on a mandatory is a hard stop unless a clarification can convert it; compute `C` share on mandatories; check deadline feasibility against the response effort (count of sections × owners available). Output `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` with the three facts that drove it. Do not soften a NO-BID.
5. **Draft clarification questions** for every `Q`, ambiguous mandatory, and scoring-rule gap. Use the question format in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §4: neutral wording, no capability reveal, one question per item, reference the clause ID. Group by theme; cap at the count the RFP allows.
6. **Build the gaps-and-risks list**: every `P` and `N` with the mitigation (partner, roadmap commitment, alternative approach, exception request) and the risk if unmitigated.
7. **Assemble the matrix** on `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` (column spec) — export as CSV/XLSX for the response team, plus a Markdown summary for the bid review. Totals by category and by compliance level must reconcile with the inventory count.
8. Run the self-check.

|---|---|---|
| Requirement inventory | `rfp-<client>-requirements.csv` | Script output, reviewed |
| Compliance matrix | `rfp-<client>-compliance-matrix.csv` (or `.xlsx` if openpyxl available) | Columns per `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` |
| Bid review summary | `rfp-<client>-bid-review.md` | Bottom line (BID call) · Totals table · Mandatory non-compliances · Gaps and risks · Clarification questions · Response plan (section, owner, due) · Administrative checklist |

## Self-check
- [ ] Inventory count = matrix row count; totals by category reconcile
- [ ] No `C` without a cited evidence item
- [ ] Every mandatory `N` or `P` appears in gaps-and-risks with a mitigation and owner
- [ ] Clarification questions reference clause IDs and reveal no capability gaps
- [ ] Bid/no-bid call on line 1 of the summary with its three drivers
- [ ] Deadlines (Q&A, submission) stated with source page
- [ ] No other-client names or internal rate information in any artifact that could ship

When to use

  • "Redline this SOW — the scope is too loose."
  • "Write acceptance criteria for these deliverables."
  • NOT for: proposal narrative (proposal-writer), estimate (effort-estimator), MSA/legal clauses (flag for counsel).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Approved proposal (final version)yesfile
Estimate output: phases, effort, team, milestonesyesfile
Commercial model decided: fixed / T&M / milestone / run-rateyesuser
Governing agreement (MSA) reference and any mandated SOW templatenouser / file
Client-side named roles for RACInouser
Existing SOW draft (redline mode)yes in redlinefile

If the proposal or commercial model is missing, ask once. An SOW without a decided commercial model cannot define acceptance and payment linkage.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. Redline convention applies in redline mode.

  1. Extract the scope baseline from the proposal: objectives, phases, deliverables, team, timeline, assumptions, risks. Build a traceability table: proposal section → SOW clause. Anything in the proposal that is not scope, deliverable, assumption, or commercial term (marketing language, win themes) is dropped from the SOW.
  2. Write scope as numbered statements per references/sow-method.md §2: each in-scope item is a verb + object + boundary ("Migrate the 42 interfaces listed in Appendix A from platform X to platform Y, including unit and integration test"). Mirror every in-scope item with an explicit out-of-scope statement where ambiguity is likely. Run the scope-ambiguity scan (§3) and register each ambiguity with its resolution.
  3. Define deliverables with acceptance criteria using references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md. Each deliverable: ID, description, format, acceptance criteria (objective, testable), acceptance method (review / test / demonstration), review window (days), deemed-acceptance rule, approver (client role).
  4. Decision point — commercial linkage. Per references/sow-method.md §5: fixed-price → milestones tied to accepted deliverables; T&M → monthly invoicing against approved timesheets with a not-to-exceed; milestone → payment on acceptance with a percentage schedule; run-rate → service levels with credits. Amounts come from the estimate/proposal pricing or are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]. Never place a number without a source.
  5. Convert every assumption into a change-control trigger: assumption → basis → what happens if false (effort, schedule, price) → who confirms by when. Client dependencies get a due date and a consequence clause ("delay of client dependency D3 by more than 5 business days shifts dependent milestones day for day").
  6. Governance and RACI: forums, cadence, decision rights, escalation path, and a RACI across the deliverables with one A per row. Client roles named if supplied, else role titles with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___].
  7. Change-control procedure: request → impact assessment (effort, schedule, price, risk) → approval authority and threshold → documentation. Include a minor-change threshold to avoid paperwork for trivial items.
  8. Legal flags: list every clause that counsel must confirm against the MSA (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance). Do not draft these; reference the MSA or mark for counsel.
  9. Redline mode: read the draft fully; score each clause against the ambiguity scan and acceptance patterns; produce [KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD] with rewritten text; deliver the clean version.
  10. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: sow-<client>-<initiative>-v0.1.md (or -redline-<date>.md in redline mode)
  • Template: assets/sow-template.md
  • Companion: assets/assumptions-checklist.md completed as Appendix C
  • Internal (not shipped): proposal→SOW traceability table; scope-ambiguity register; legal-flags list

Self-check

  • [ ] Every in-scope item is numbered, bounded, and has a matching out-of-scope statement where ambiguity exists
  • [ ] Every deliverable has objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver, deemed-acceptance rule
  • [ ] Every assumption states consequence if false and is a change-control trigger
  • [ ] Client dependencies have due dates and delay consequences
  • [ ] Payment schedule links to accepted deliverables/milestones; all amounts sourced or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
  • [ ] RACI has exactly one A per deliverable
  • [ ] Legal clauses referenced to MSA or flagged for counsel; none drafted here
  • [ ] No proposal marketing language, no other-client references, no author history

References

  • references/sow-method.md — scope statements, ambiguity scan, commercial linkage, change control, governance
  • references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md — patterns by deliverable type with examples
  • assets/sow-template.md — SOW template
  • assets/assumptions-checklist.md — assumptions and dependencies checklist by engagement type

4. **Decision point — commercial linkage.** Per `references/sow-method.md` §5: fixed-price → milestones tied to accepted deliverables; T&M → monthly invoicing against approved timesheets with a not-to-exceed; milestone → payment on acceptance with a percentage schedule; run-rate → service levels with credits. Amounts come from the estimate/proposal pricing or are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never place a number without a source.
5. **Convert every assumption into a change-control trigger**: assumption → basis → what happens if false (effort, schedule, price) → who confirms by when. Client dependencies get a due date and a consequence clause ("delay of client dependency D3 by more than 5 business days shifts dependent milestones day for day").
6. **Governance and RACI**: forums, cadence, decision rights, escalation path, and a RACI across the deliverables with one A per row. Client roles named if supplied, else role titles with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
7. **Change-control procedure**: request → impact assessment (effort, schedule, price, risk) → approval authority and threshold → documentation. Include a minor-change threshold to avoid paperwork for trivial items.
8. **Legal flags**: list every clause that counsel must confirm against the MSA (IP, liability, warranties, termination, data protection, non-solicit, insurance). Do not draft these; reference the MSA or mark for counsel.
9. **Redline mode**: read the draft fully; score each clause against the ambiguity scan and acceptance patterns; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` with rewritten text; deliver the clean version.
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `sow-<client>-<initiative>-v0.1.md` (or `-redline-<date>.md` in redline mode)
- Template: `assets/sow-template.md`
- Companion: `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` completed as Appendix C
- Internal (not shipped): proposal→SOW traceability table; scope-ambiguity register; legal-flags list

## Self-check
- [ ] Every in-scope item is numbered, bounded, and has a matching out-of-scope statement where ambiguity exists
- [ ] Every deliverable has objective acceptance criteria, method, review window, approver, deemed-acceptance rule
- [ ] Every assumption states consequence if false and is a change-control trigger
- [ ] Client dependencies have due dates and delay consequences
- [ ] Payment schedule links to accepted deliverables/milestones; all amounts sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] RACI has exactly one A per deliverable
- [ ] Legal clauses referenced to MSA or flagged for counsel; none drafted here
- [ ] No proposal marketing language, no other-client references, no author history

## References
- `references/sow-method.md` — scope statements, ambiguity scan, commercial linkage, change control, governance
- `references/acceptance-criteria-patterns.md` — patterns by deliverable type with examples
- `assets/sow-template.md` — SOW template
- `assets/assumptions-checklist.md` — assumptions and dependencies checklist by engagement type
